name: record_session
description: Persist one practice session in the learner's six databases at once (update-db.py's report in the self-hosted mode): a session_end, a role-play's debrief, a town check sent, a writing exercise in chat. Call it once per session, at its end; the same session_id again replaces that session. Take session_id from learner_state's next_session_id (another language's: learner_state with its language, and language here). The app persists reviews, packs, readings and dialog words itself: don't record those events. review_results run SM-2 on cards already in the deck; quality 0-5 = floor(score / 2): 5 perfect, 4 right after a hesitation, 3 right with difficulty, 2 wrong but remembered when shown, 1 wrong but familiar, 0 blackout. Below 3 the card starts over. A right answer looked up on the cheat sheet is at most 4. errors: one per distinct mistake, your_answer exactly as the learner had it.

session_id.description: learner_state's next_session_id: session-NNN, or session-<code>-NNN in another language. Ignored with record_session false.

language.description: Another language than the home one (a code such as "it", or a name): the report goes to that language's databases. Omit for the home language.

record_session.description: false: only add new_vocabulary as review items, no session (no minutes, no streak day); then no practice fields.

skill_scores.description: Per skill (vocabulary, grammar, writing, speaking, reading, listening): exercises done and how many were right (a count, not a percentage).

errors.description: One entry per distinct mistake (collapse duplicates of a pattern_id). The app builds the learner's own traps from them.

pattern_id.description: The mistake pattern's id (an existing one from learner_state when it fits).

category.description: grammar, formal_informal, vocabulary, spelling, prepositions, articles, missing, …

subcategory.description: e.g. verb_conjugation; "listening" for a hearing slip.

your_answer.description: Exactly as the learner had it.

correct_answer.description: The right sentence (parts of one example joined with " / ", notes in brackets).

new_vocabulary.description: Items the learner met for the first time: new review cards, due tomorrow. An item that exists is left as it is.

content.description: The front: the answer, in the target language.

answer.description: The back: the meaning, the prompt; (…) is a note.

example.description: The sentence it was met in.

review_results.description: Cards already in the deck that were answered: SM-2 runs on each.

gentle.description: A word got wrong in a dialog: lowered gently, no review (its quality is ignored).

milestones.description: Each a string, or {milestone, date?}: a session-log milestone and an achievement.

level.description: The report's language's new current level: only for a real placement or a correction (a level-up is the app's treasure map).
